numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Numerical-precision error in the computed `theta` component when converting from `CylindricalRepresentation` to `PhysicsSphericalRepresentation` for vectors very close to the Z axis.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Compute `theta` using the numerically stable expression `np.arctan2(self.rho, self.z)` instead of `np.arccos(self.z / r)`.
trigger_conditions: Vectors very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds) when converting from `CylindricalRepresentation` to `PhysicsSphericalRepresentation`.
Case where the previous formula `np.arccos(self.z / r)` suffers numerical precision issues for those near-axis inputs.

input_output_examples.input: CylindricalRepresentation with `rho`/`z` values corresponding to a vector very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds).

oracle_clues: The change explicitly replaces `theta=np.arccos(self.z / r)` with `theta=np.arctan2(self.rho, self.z)`.
The bugfix notes it is a numerical-precision bug for vectors very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds).

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: vectors very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds); also exemplified by CylindricalRepresentation(rho=1 * u.m, z=1e8 * u.m) producing small theta=1e-8 * u.rad
category_specific_evidence: Fixed a numerical-precision bug with the calculation of the ``theta`` component when converting from ``CylindricalRepresentation`` to ``PhysicsSphericalRepresentation`` for vectors very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds).
Conversion change: cylindrical.py uses `theta=np.arccos(self.z / r)` previously, now `theta=np.arctan2(self.rho, self.z)`.
Added test `test_to_physicsspherical_small_theta`: `cyl = CylindricalRepresentation(rho=1 * u.m, phi=10 * u.deg, z=1e8 * u.m)` and checks `got.theta` is `1e-8 * u.rad` using `assert_allclose`.
Test also asserts `got.r == 1e8 * u.m` and `got.phi == 10 * u.deg` with `assert_allclose`.
The transformation accuracy target is explicitly described as being accurate for small theta (`test_to_physicsspherical_small_theta`).
reproduction_risks: Reproduction may need the specific near-Z-axis regime mentioned (within milliarcseconds / very small theta) to trigger the precision discrepancy.

Any tolerance parameters for pass/fail are not specified beyond use of `assert_allclose`, so matching the exact separation threshold may require knowing default `assert_allclose` tolerances used by the test suite (not provided here).
